HCBCOGN312.name: Psycholinguistics

HCBCOGN312.topics: Psycholinguistics is the study of the neurobiological and psychological factors that enable us to acquire, use, and understand language. Modern research draws on cognitive psychology, neuroscience, and computer science to investigate how language is processed. The course focuses primarily, though not exclusively, on the neuroscience of language. Students examine theoretical and experimental issues in speech production and comprehension, language impairments, the relationship between thought and language, and the evolution and acquisition of language. They also gain hands-on experience with experimental approaches to the study of language and develop an understanding of human linguistic capacity as a subject of multidisciplinary research. Topics covered: What is language? Evolutionary aspects of language and animal communication; language and thought; aphasia; language acquisition; bilingualism; speech comprehension; semantics; reading and dyslexia; speech production.

analysis: The closest plan connects eight core interests through programming, algorithms, logic and statistics, agents, machine learning, deep learning, robot sensing and control, cognition, psycholinguistics and responsible design. Linear Systems replaces health psychology and provides concrete signal, filtering and feedback methods useful in robotics and perception. Persuasion remains a complementary course on human influence and framing. The software route builds learning and autonomous systems from programming, advanced algorithms, numerical methods, probability, databases and systems through implemented learning agents and robotics. Business & Economy in the Age of AI adds study of agentic AI, business deployment, accountability and regulation in place of general persuasion. The reasoning and cognition direction develops computational inference and logic alongside language, perception, social and developmental psychology, philosophical analysis and behavioural evidence synthesis. Introductory philosophy replaces persuasion and provides groundwork in knowledge, agency and consciousness. Psycholinguistics follows the brain and behaviour gateway in the only planned spring term, with introductory neurobiology in the same term. Both cognitive plans retain subsequent perception and cognition. The selected options differ by seven, six and eleven courses (52.5, 45 and 82.5 EC). UCR’s logic, automata and algorithmic thinking contribute to formal reasoning, but do not reproduce Utrecht’s advanced logic and knowledge representation. Neural networks include transformers and text generation, while UCR psycholinguistics studies human language experimentally; no dedicated computational language processing course is implied. The experimental psycholinguistics placement now reflects the closer match. The fourth, Cognitive Processing, has genuine UCR content but overlaps the chosen cognition directions and falls beyond the three-option cap.

alignment.rationale: Both develop programming and computational problem-solving. UCR uses Python.
Both study methods for intelligent systems. UCR focuses on probabilistic decision-making under uncertainty.
Both study data structures, algorithms and computational complexity.
Both teach machine-learning methods and model evaluation. UCR covers regression, classification and unsupervised learning.
UCR studies transformers and language applications within a broader neural networks course. Utrecht provides a dedicated language models course.
UCR develops advanced learning through reinforcement learning and implementing agents. Utrecht’s course covers a broader set of advanced machine-learning methods.
Both teach mathematics for modelling. UCR focuses on calculus, equations and dynamic models.
Both develop formal logic for computing and AI. UCR also covers discrete structures and proof techniques.
Both develop statistical and experimental methods for empirical research.
Both introduce human cognition and ways to study it. UCR also gives an introduction to neuroanatomy and behaviour.
Both study language processing and how to investigate it. UCR emphasises the psychology and neuroscience of language.
Utrecht builds computational models of language processing. UCR studies language applications within deep learning and human language in psycholinguistics.
Both consider philosophical questions about intelligence and mind. UCR also studies identity and conscious experience.
Both consider philosophical questions about AI. UCR focuses on issues such as fairness, privacy, agency and responsibility.
Utrecht provides a dedicated course on formal and natural languages. UCR covers related formal tools within logic and algorithms.
Utrecht devotes a course to connections between natural processes and computation.
Utrecht provides a dedicated advanced logic course. UCR develops formal reasoning within logic and algorithms.
Utrecht requires a supervised thesis after preparation in experimental methods. UCR offers optional independent research outside these schedules.
Utrecht leaves 45 EC for profiling, such as a minor or electives, subject to programme requirements.
